key_pattern: The modern catalogue preserves the same four semantic categories named in 1864 item 12 across English, Farsi, Urdu and Nepali/Khas documentary states. Farsi vol.101 items 4, 8 and 9 are especially striking because they cover judicial system, thar classification and customs respectively, all on machine-made paper.
interpretation: The multilingual companion ecology strengthens the identification of 1864 item 12 as a version family rather than a simple subject bundle. It also suggests that modern 1921 volumes 56/60/101/103 may contain companion states dispersed from the same or closely related transfer family. Direct historical container labels are still required for identity-level mapping.
source_control_rules: Do not translate the manifest's label 'Persian' automatically into modern catalogue 'Urdu'. Preserve the mismatch until scripts/texts are physically compared.
Topic overlap and Cambridge cross-reference establish version-family proximity, not 1864 co-custody identity by themselves.
Modern vol.101 adjacency is produced by later archival arrangement and cannot be treated as original item-12 adjacency.
Khas in the 1864 manifest is a historical language label; modern catalogue Nepali/Khas attribution must be controlled object by object.
The strongest direct historical identifier remains vol.6 Box 2 / Item 12.
next_actions: Inspect RAS BHH/11/14 and BHH/19/5 item 12 for wording, sub-list references and annotations.
Inspect vol.101 items 4, 8 and 9 for old cover/bundle/container marks and compare handwriting/title layers.
Trace the army companion named as Persian in 1864: search Farsi/Urdu army papers for old titles or cross-references to the English item-12 family.
Compare vol.56/2 and vol.60/7 title/cover metadata with the old item-12 Khas-paper statement.
